endpoint.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was time to sputum culture conversion (SCC), used as a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit under accelerated approval.

citations.quote: C208 Stage 2 is considered the pivotal trial for this application, with C208 Stage 1 and C209 providing supportive evidence. Analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint, time to SCC, for C208 Stage 2, demonstrated a median time of 83 days for the bedaquiline treatment group (95% CI: 56, 97) compared to 125 days for the placebo group (95% CI: 98, 168).

result.text: Median time to SCC 83 days (bedaquiline) vs 125 days (placebo). Week 24 culture conversion treatment success 52 (79%) vs 38 (58%), difference 21% [95% CI 5.7%, 36.7%], p=0.008.

target_moa.text: Bedaquiline is a diarylquinoline antimycobacterial drug that inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase, an enzyme essential for generation of energy in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

citations.quote: Bedaquiline is a diarylquinoline antimycobacterial drug that inhibits mycobacterial ATP (adenosine 5'-triphosphate) synthase, an enzyme that is essential for the generation of energy in *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*.
Bedaquiline is a diarylquinoline antimycobacterial drug [see *Microbiology* (12.4)].

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%): nausea (38.0% vs 32.1% placebo), arthralgia (32.9% vs 22.2%), and headache (27.8% vs 12.3%); also hemoptysis and chest pain. Most serious: increased mortality in the SIRTURO group (9/79, 11.4%) vs placebo (2/81, 2.5%), and QT prolongation.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions reported in \ge10% of patients treated with SIRTURO are nausea, arthralgia, and headache.
Additional adverse events reported in \ge10% of patients treated with SIRTURO and with a higher frequency than the placebo treatment group are hemoptysis and chest pain. (6)

An increased risk of death was seen in the SIRTURO treatment group (9/79, 11.4%) compared to the placebo treatment group (2/81, 2.5%) in one placebo-controlled trial. Only use SIRTURO when an effective treatment regimen cannot otherwise be provided.
QT prolongation can occur with SIRTURO. Use with drugs that prolong the QT interval may cause additive QT prolongation.

detail.text: Boxed warning: increased risk of death in the SIRTURO group (9/79, 11.4%) vs placebo (2/81, 2.5%) in one placebo-controlled trial—only use when an effective treatment regimen cannot otherwise be provided; and QT prolongation, which may be additive with other QT-prolonging drugs.

description.text: Converted Sirturo (bedaquiline) from accelerated approval to full approval for MDR-TB combination therapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for conversion of Sirturo from accelerated approval to full approval. Sirturo is indicated as part of combination therapy in the treatment of adult and pediatric patients (5 years and older and weighing at least 15 kg) with pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) due to *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* resistant to at least rifampin and isoniazid. The following sections of the prescribing information (PI) have been revised: **HIGHLIGHTS OF PRESCRIBING INFORMATION**, **BOXED WARNING**, **INDICATIONS AND USAGE (1)**, **DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION (2)**, **WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS (5)**, **ADVERSE REACTIONS (6)**, **DRUG INTERACTIONS (7)**, **CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY (12)**, **CLINICAL STUDIES (14)** and **PATIENT COUNSELING INFORMATION (17)**.
